When are two geometric vectors considered equal?
choices: When they have both the same magnitude and the same direction
When they have the same initial point
When their lengths are equal regardless of direction
questions.answer: Vectors are defined strictly by magnitude and direction, independent of their initial position in space.

questions.q: Find the unit vector $\mathbf{u}$ in the same direction as $\mathbf{v} = \langle 5, -12 \rangle$.
What is the result of multiplying any vector $\mathbf{v}$ by scalar $-1$?
choices: A vector of the same magnitude pointing in the exactly opposite direction
questions.answer: Scalar multiplication by $-1$ negates every component, reversing the direction while preserving the magnitude.

questions.q: Two forces act on an object: $\mathbf{F}_1 = \langle 20, 0 \rangle\text{ N}$ and $\mathbf{F}_2 = \langle 0, 15 \rangle\text{ N}$. Find the magnitude of the resultant force.
An airplane flies at a heading due east with airspeed $400\text{ mph}$. A wind blows from the south at $50\text{ mph}$. Find the ground speed of the plane.
questions.answer: Plane velocity $\mathbf{v}_p = \langle 400, 0 \rangle$. Wind velocity (blowing from south means heading north) $\mathbf{v}_w = \langle 0, 50 \rangle$. Total $\|\mathbf{v}\| = \sqrt{160000 + 2500} = \sqrt{162500} \approx 403.1\text{ mph}$.
